tasks.short: Prepare computer science syllabi, assignments and handouts.

steps.what: Choose learning outcomes and verify current course facts, source materials and student prerequisites
inputs: actual course requirements and timetable
approved prior materials and technical references
outputs: teacher-checked course source set and instructional choices

steps.what: Populate exact syllabus fields and selected reusable material in native course templates
inputs: teacher-checked course source set and instructional choices
approved material identifiers and course template

steps.what: Draft and correct new assignment explanations and handout prose against the checked source set
inputs: source-linked factual course material draft
teacher-checked course source set and instructional choices

loop.purpose: Draft variable explanations for teacher-selected computing concepts
loop.input: approved technical sources, learning outcomes and factual template draft
loop.output: candidate assignment and handout prose with source references
loop.check: Teacher checks concept accuracy, prerequisites, every instruction, omissions and correspondence of claims to actual technical sources; corrects all examples
loop.stop: Missing source or two failed corrections returns drafting to teacher
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates handle fixed course facts first; new explanatory prose varies by concept and learner level

steps.what: Test code examples and approve the complete final syllabus, assignments and handouts
inputs: complete corrected course material draft
teacher-checked course source set and instructional choices
outputs: approved final course materials and course destination

steps.what: Save the approved final course materials to the course record
inputs: approved final course materials and course destination

tasks.design: Configure {LMS} templates for exact course fields and existing selected materials before adding a bounded prose drafting loop. OTHER is the existing code execution environment used by the teacher to check examples. The teacher selects content, corrects all prose and tests examples before final approval; same-system save earns no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exact course facts and new explanatory prose may be assembled manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates reuse checked facts; bounded drafting can propose variable explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Designing a valid assignment and ensuring examples teach the intended concept.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher judges prerequisites, difficulty and pedagogical value.
tasks.altitude: Teacher-designed materials with reusable facts and checked drafting.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native course templates reuse exact fields and a bounded model can draft explanatory prose subject to full teacher correction.

assumptions: All effort shares are provisional, not observed baselines. Existing native assembly and code runtime receive no new benefit.

Teacher captures/checks course_id, learning_outcomes, prerequisites, dates, assessment_rules and selected_material_ids in s1 at full time. Registrar supplies existing timetable; teacher supplies authoritative concept sources. Missing facts or sources require manual drafting.

s3 retains 18 hours for complete semantic correction, s4 retains 29 for running/checking examples and final pedagogical approval. No autonomous code publication occurs; save is unchanged. Distribution outside the saved course record is not claimed.
unknowns: Residual assembly after current LMS templates
research_questions: Do fully corrected drafts save teacher effort on real computing materials after native templates?

incremental.description: Audit technical draft errors and maintain course template/source mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 complete tested final course materials and course destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 20 factual assembly and 12 corrected prose hours less 2 upkeep = 30. Low halves factual assembly only and keeps prose manual: 10 minus 2 = 8.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade computer science examinations.

steps.what: Compile the examination, closed-item keys and open-answer rubric and verify test validity
inputs: learning outcomes
actual approved item bank and course content

steps.what: Administer the examination and address actual student and procedural issues
inputs: teacher-checked examination, keys and rubric
actual students
outputs: actual submitted examination answers and administration issues

steps.what: Apply exact closed-item keys and inspect exceptions using native examination marking
inputs: actual submitted examination answers and administration issues
teacher-checked examination, keys and rubric
outputs: teacher-checked closed-item mark suggestions and exceptions

steps.what: Grade open answers and resolve closed-item exceptions using academic judgement
inputs: actual submitted examination answers and administration issues
teacher-checked closed-item mark suggestions and exceptions
teacher-checked examination, keys and rubric

steps.what: Check every final result, student identity and marking exception and approve the final register
inputs: teacher-assigned candidate examination results
actual submitted examination answers and administration issues

steps.what: Commit the approved final examination result register
inputs: approved final examination result register

tasks.design: Configure {EXAM_PLATFORM} native exact-key marking, represented by LMS. The teacher compiles and administers the examination, checks suggested closed-item marks, grades open answers and approves every final result. No model grades or detects cheating. Existing same-system result commit earns no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed-item scores may still be compared and totalled manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native examination platforms support exact-key marking.
tasks.still_hard: Valid examinations, open-answer interpretation and resolving irregularities.
tasks.human_edge: The authorised examiner sets results and handles context-sensitive exceptions.
tasks.altitude: Human examination decisions with exact closed-item assistance.

evidence.claim: Examination tools support automatic marking of closed questions and item statistics.

assumptions: Provisional shares assume an examination containing closed and open answers; measure the actual mix and existing native marking. Already automatic scoring earns no new benefit.

Teacher authors and checks item_id, accepted_answer, points and rubric in s1 at full time. Students supply actual answers in s2 through the existing platform, not new focal-role capture work. Missing keys, ambiguous answers or unmatched student IDs require manual marking.

s3 retains 8 hours for inspecting marks and exceptions; s4 and s5 retain full examiner judgement and final checking. The result commit is unchanged; no cross-system grade re-keying or student notification is claimed.
research_questions: Which closed-item scores are still manually checked or totalled after existing examination functions?

incremental.description: Audit exact-key mappings and exception handling

approvals.approved_version: s5 complete final result register with student identities

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only exact-key marking changes: 20 times 60% = 12 hours less 1 upkeep = 11. Low halves this benefit: 6 minus 1 = 5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver lectures on programming, data structures and software design.

steps.what: Choose lecture aims and verify the technical sources and examples to teach
inputs: actual course outcomes and student prerequisites
approved technical sources and prior lecture material
outputs: teacher-checked lecture source set and selected examples

steps.what: Assemble lecture structure and selected diagrams using native presentation and course templates
inputs: teacher-checked lecture source set and selected examples
approved reusable diagrams and lecture template

steps.what: Run code examples and correct and approve the complete final lecture material
inputs: candidate lecture material
teacher-checked lecture source set and selected examples

steps.what: Save the approved final lecture material in the course record
inputs: approved final lecture material

steps.what: Deliver the lecture and respond to actual programming and design questions
inputs: saved final lecture material
actual student questions and responses
outputs: actual lecture and observed learning difficulties

steps.what: Write and approve actual lecture observations and needed teaching adjustments
inputs: actual lecture and observed learning difficulties

steps.what: Save the approved final actual lecture note
inputs: approved final actual lecture note

tasks.design: Configure native {PRESENTATION_TOOL} and {LMS} templates for selected existing lecture material. OTHER is the teachers existing code execution environment. The teacher chooses concepts, tests examples and delivers the lecture. Actual lecture notes follow delivery; both separate same-system saves earn no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated slide and diagram assembly may consume preparation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates reuse selected material without replacing technical or pedagogical decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining abstract concepts and responding to confusion.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher adapts explanations to actual student understanding.
tasks.altitude: Live computer science teaching with reusable material assembly.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native presentation and course templates can reuse approved lecture diagrams and structure.

assumptions: All effort shares are provisional; credit only remaining repetitive assembly after current native templates.

Teacher selects source_version, example_id and diagram_id in s1 at full time; current source files already exist. s2 retains 12 hours for assembly choices and adaptation, while s3 retains complete example checking. Missing suitable material uses manual preparation.

s6 captures actual topic, observed_difficulty and next_adjustment after delivery at full time. Live explanation, questions and code runtime receive no automation saving; save actions are fully retained.
research_questions: Which lecture preparation actions still repeat existing material after the current presentation tools?

incremental.description: Maintain reusable lecture templates and diagram references

approvals.approved_version: s3 complete tested final lecture material

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only assembly changes: 20 times 40% = 8 hours less 1 upkeep = 7. Low halves assembly benefit: 4 minus 1 = 3.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade computer science work, laboratory assignments and papers.

steps.what: Inspect submitted work and apply teacher-defined exact tests and format checks
inputs: actual student submissions
existing teacher-validated tests and assignment requirements
outputs: checked test evidence and identified exceptions

steps.what: Evaluate reasoning, software design, laboratory work and papers against the academic rubric
inputs: actual student submissions
checked test evidence and identified exceptions
teacher-approved rubric
outputs: teacher-assigned marks and specific evidence notes

steps.what: Draft feedback from the teachers marks and evidence and correct it against submissions
inputs: teacher-assigned marks and specific evidence notes
actual student submissions
teacher-approved rubric
outputs: complete corrected feedback and assigned mark draft

loop.purpose: Phrase formative feedback from teacher-authored judgements without changing marks
loop.input: actual submission, rubric, teacher-assigned mark and evidence notes
loop.output: candidate feedback linked to actual submission passages
loop.check: Teacher checks every criticism and recommendation against code or text, omissions, consistency with the rubric and unchanged marks; corrects all feedback
loop.stop: Unsupported criticism or two failed corrections returns feedback writing to teacher
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates handle fixed fields; variable feedback wording depends on the teachers specific evidence and needs semantic checking

steps.what: Approve each complete final mark and feedback record against the actual student work
inputs: complete corrected feedback and assigned mark draft
actual student submissions
outputs: approved final mark and feedback register

steps.what: Save the approved final mark and feedback register
inputs: approved final mark and feedback register
outputs: saved final work grades and feedback

tasks.design: Configure existing {AUTOGRADER} exact tests and checks, denoted OTHER, before bounded feedback wording in {LMS}. The teacher inspects test evidence, evaluates all work and sets every grade. The model only phrases teacher-authored judgements, with full correction and final approval. Same-system grade save earns no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some exact checks and evidence-based feedback wording may still be repeated manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exact checks and feedback drafting from instructor notes can assist separate parts of marking.
tasks.still_hard: Judging reasoning, originality, design quality and experimental understanding.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher interprets learning demonstrated by the whole submission.
tasks.altitude: Teacher grading with checked evidence and draft feedback.

evidence.claim: Feedback systems can draft text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
Model knowledge: configured assignment tests can check exact code outputs, while design and reasoning still need examiner judgement.

assumptions: All shares are provisional for a mixed computing-work batch; measure actual checkable work and current automatic checks. Existing autograding, compilation and test runtime receive no new benefit.

Students produce actual submission files through existing LMS capture. Teacher supplies and validates tests, expected_outputs and rubric in normal assignment design; recurring upkeep is counted below. s1 retains input checking, running setup and exception inspection. Missing tests or unsupported file types require manual checks.

s2 captures student_id, assigned_mark, rubric_item and actual evidence at full time. s3 retains 12 hours for complete semantic correction, s4 retains 19 for every final mark/feedback review. The model cannot assign marks or infer misconduct. Grade save is fully retained.
research_questions: Does fully corrected feedback drafting reduce total marker effort after existing tests and templates?

incremental.description: Audit feedback errors and maintain validated exact-check mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 every final teacher-assigned mark and corrected feedback with student IDs

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 10 residual exact-check hours and 8 feedback wording hours minus 2 upkeep = 16. Low halves only exact-check benefit and keeps feedback manual: 5 minus 2 = 3.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Academic judgement and live teaching with checked preparation and marking assistance.
reach: Less repeated course assembly and exact checking
role.ambitious_version: The teacher keeps all grades, pedagogical decisions and student interaction while reducing genuinely residual copying, checking and wording work.
